findings.title: robots.txt has no deliberate per-purpose agent policy (single `*` group)
findings.evidence: live `/robots.txt` 2026-10-12 (`$S/robots.txt`, 3,644 B, `content-type: text/plain`, etag `RobotsController`): exactly two groups, `User-agent: *` (`Allow: /` plus ~20 Allow and ~40 Disallow rules) and `User-agent: adsbot-google`; `grep -c "Content-Signal"` = 0; none of GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, CCBot is named; no `Agentmap:`. The file is Shopify's current default (comment header "Shopify storefront … Agent instructions: https://primesupplements.ro/agents.md"), i.e. the store has never expressed a policy of its own: training, search and user-triggered access are all "allowed by omission".
findings.affected_scope: whole site (1,151 sitemap URLs incl. the /ro-hu/ duplicates) and the B2B store (its own default robots.txt). - Recommendation (merchant-controlled; Shopify supports `templates/robots.txt.liquid`): keep Shopify's default groups via the `robots.default_groups` loop and add (a) Content-Signal to the `*` group (AGENTIC-02) and (b) explicit groups for search and user-triggered agents so the policy is a decision, not an omission. Training (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `Google-Extended`) is a business choice
findings.recommendation: (merchant-controlled; Shopify supports `templates/robots.txt.liquid`): keep Shopify's default groups via the `robots.default_groups` loop and add (a) Content-Signal to the `*` group (AGENTIC-02) and (b) explicit groups for search and user-triggered agents so the policy is a decision, not an omission. Training (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `Google-Extended`) is a business choice: ask the owner; do not block by default. Because a named group replaces `*` for that bot (RFC 9309), every named group must repeat the private-path Disallows. Draft: ```liquid {%- comment -%} templates/robots.txt.liquid {%- endcomment -%} {%- for group in robots.default_groups -%} {{- group.user_agent }} {%- if group.user_agent.value == '*' %} Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no {%- comment -%} ai-train value = owner decision {%- endcomment -%} {%- endif -%} {%- for rule in group.rules %} {{ rule }} {%- endfor -%} {%- if group.sitemap != blank %} {{ group.sitemap }} {%- endif -%} {%- endfor %} User-agent: OAI-SearchBot User-agent: ChatGPT-User User-agent: Claude-SearchBot User-agent: Claude-User User-agent: PerplexityBot User-agent: Perplexity-User Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no Allow: / Disallow: /cart/ Disallow: /checkout Disallow: /checkouts/ Disallow: /orders Disallow: /account Disallow: /collections/*sort_by* Disallow: /collections/*filter*&*filter* ``` Keep `/ro-hu/` variants of each Disallow if the Hungary market stays (see TECH findings on the duplicate market). `Google-Agent` generally ignores robots.txt, so no line is needed; the private paths are already behind authentication.
findings.falsifiability: `curl -s https://primesupplements.ro/robots.txt | grep -E "^User-agent|^Content-Signal"` shows the new groups and lines; a parse with `agentic_check.py` (`robots-ai-groups`) lists one group per purpose.
findings.leading_indicator: robots.txt served from the theme template (etag changes; file contains the custom groups) within minutes of publishing the theme.

findings.title: No Content-Signal anywhere (robots.txt, HTTP header or meta)
findings.evidence: `grep -c Content-Signal $S/robots.txt` = 0; response headers of `/`, `/robots.txt`, `/llms.txt`, `/products.json`, `/api/ucp/mcp` contain no `content-signal`; `meta_content_signal = 0` on all 10 analysed pages (`$S/a11y-proxy.json`). `agentic_fix.py robots --file` produced `$S/robots-draft.txt`, whose only difference from the live file is two inserted lines (after line 18 in the `*` group and after line 92 in the adsbot group): `Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no`.

findings.title: Shopify bot protection challenges moderate-rate agent traffic with 429 "Verifying your connection..."; no merchant allowlist
findings.evidence:
during recon (same day, ~15 requests in quick succession from one IP with a Chrome UA) `/search?q=creatina` and the B2B home came back as the Cloudflare-injected challenge page: `$R/pages/search-creatina.html` (9,435 B) and `$R/pages/page-b2b.html` (9,424 B) both have `Verifying your connection...`, `

Your connection needs to be verified before you can proceed

`, `cf-injected-html`, ``, `lang="en"`. The context file records 429 status for these. A single throttled request today returned 200 for `/search?q=creatina` (410,360 B, title "Căutare: s-au găsit 32 rezultate pentru „creatina”"). `agents.md`/`llms.txt` also warn "The MCP endpoint is rate-limited per IP". Context: Bytespider receives 429 by Shopify default.
findings.affected_scope: every HTML URL (1,151 sitemap URLs + /search + B2B store) for any client that fetches faster than Shopify's threshold — typically an agent comparing several products or paginating the 33-page blog; the challenge page is English-only, has no content and requires JS, so an agent sees nothing.
findings.recommendation: the WAF is Shopify's (merchant cannot allowlist verified bots, tune thresholds or disable challenges on Online Store). What the merchant controls: (1) keep the sanctioned low-cost surfaces healthy and advertised — `/products.json`, `/collections/{handle}/products.json`, the UCP `search_catalog` tool — and reference them in the theme footer/"Pentru asistenți AI" page (AGENTIC-04); (2) do not add app-level bot blockers or extra CAPTCHAs; (3) reduce the number of requests an agent needs per task: fix the /ro-hu/ duplicate market (halves the crawl surface, see TECH), add blog tag/category hubs so the 354 articles are reachable in ≤3 hops instead of 33 paginated pages; (4) watch Shopify Analytics → "Online store sessions by traffic source"/bot reports for 429 volume. Treat this as "behaviour toward unverified traffic": whether signed (Web Bot Auth) agents are exempted at Shopify's edge is undocumented.
findings.falsifiability: a controlled test of 20 product URLs at 1 request/s with a normal UA returns 200 throughout (no challenge); UCP `search_catalog` answers under the same load.
findings.leading_indicator: share of 429 responses in Shopify's bot analytics; fewer "Verifying your connection" pages seen by agents.

findings.title: No Markdown delivery; a strict `Accept: text/markdown` request gets a 404 instead of the HTML page
findings.evidence: (live 2026-10-12): `GET /products/baton-proteic-capsuni` with `Accept: text/markdown` → **404**, `content-type: text/plain`, body `Not Found` (9 B) (`$S/md-accept.headers`, `$R/pages/md-product.txt`); `/products/baton-proteic-capsuni.md` → 404 `Not Found`; with `Accept: text/markdown, text/html;q=0.9, */*;q=0.8` → 200 HTML 344,013 B. `Vary: Accept` is sent on every response. No `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">` on any analysed page (`link_alternate_markdown = 0`), no `Link: …; rel="alternate"; type="text/markdown"`.
findings.recommendation: Shopify Online Store cannot serve a `text/markdown` representation (Liquid templates are always `text/html`; root `.md` files cannot be hosted; the 404-on-strict-Accept is Shopify's content negotiation and cannot be configured). Record it as not feasible on this platform; the agent-friendly text channels that do exist are `/products/{handle}.json` (clean JSON, product `body_html`) and the UCP `get_product` tool. No consumer agent is publicly confirmed to send `Accept: text/markdown`, so no traffic is lost today. If the store ever moves to Hydrogen/Oxygen or puts its own Cloudflare zone in front, enable Markdown negotiation there (reference config in the skill).
findings.falsifiability: `curl -sI -H "Accept: text/markdown" https://primesupplements.ro/products/baton-proteic-capsuni | grep -iE "^HTTP|content-type"` returns 200 `text/markdown` after a platform change.

findings.title: Product photos are nameless in the accessibility tree (empty alt on 493/493 product images)
findings.evidence: product page `/products/baton-proteic-capsuni`: 6 of 27 `` have `alt=""` — the two logos and the gallery images `files/1.jpg`, `files/2.jpg` … (`grep ']*alt=""'`); same 6 on the creatina and MNX pages; home 24/127 empty (product-card images), collection pudra-proteica 8/23, collection all 8/52, article 4/9 (featured + body images). Root cause: Shopify product images carry no alt (context: 493/493 images on 185 products), so `snippets/product-card.liquid` and the gallery print `alt=""`, and agents reading the tree get `image` with no name; vision agents get no caption to match with the DOM.
findings.affected_scope: 185 products (493 images), 41 product cards on the home page, every collection grid.
findings.recommendation: bulk-set alt via Admin API `productUpdateMedia`/CSV (merchant-controlled, no theme change): pattern `"{product.title} – {brand} – imagine {n}"` for supplements (e.g. "Baton proteic căpșuni – Prime Supplements – ambalaj"), `"{product.title} – {colour} – față/spate"` for MNX apparel; keep decorative duplicates `alt=""`. Keep the logo link name as is (it already has an sr-only/aria name).
findings.falsifiability: `curl -s https://primesupplements.ro/products/baton-proteic-capsuni | grep -c 'alt=""'` drops from 6 to 2 (logos); `/products.json` shows `alt` on every image.
findings.leading_indicator: `images_without_alt` in `$R/shopify/products-all.json` → 0 after the bulk update.

findings.title: Viewport locks zoom (`maximum-scale=1.0, minimum-scale=1.0`)
findings.evidence: `$R/theme/layout__theme.liquid` line 17: `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, height=device-height, minimum-scale=1.0, maximum-scale=1.0">`; `viewport_blocks_zoom = True` on all 10 pages. Not one of the 33 agent-tree rules, but axe `meta-viewport` (accessibility category) fails, WCAG 1.4.4 is violated, and screenshot-based agents that zoom to read small controls (24×24 px target rule) cannot.
findings.recommendation: change to `content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"` in `layout/theme.liquid` (Impact theme; the edit survives theme updates only if re-applied — note it in the theme change log).
findings.falsifiability: Lighthouse accessibility `meta-viewport` passes; pinch-zoom works on mobile.
findings.leading_indicator: the meta tag in the live HTML.

findings.title: Page weight and control count make the DOM channel expensive for agents (345–630 KB HTML, 69–71 scripts, 128 buttons for ~700–2,800 words)
findings.evidence: (`$S/a11y-proxy.json`): home 630,754 B, 69 `<script>` (20 external), 128 buttons, 195 links, 13 forms (9 hidden quick-buy `/cart/add` forms, 3 `/localization`, 1 newsletter), 43 distinct custom elements, 106 `<svg>`, main text 2,794 words; product page 345,073 B, 71 scripts, 46 buttons, 99 links, 7 forms (3 `/localization`, 3 `/cart/add`), 37 custom elements, main text 717 words (≈1.5 % of the bytes are the words an agent needs); collection "all" 440,677 B with 15 forms; live `/search` 410,360 B with 17 forms and 78 buttons. App embeds in the HTML: judgeme (117 `jdgm` matches on home), koala-upsell-gift, pop-convert, dondy-whatsapp, affliate-by-secomapp, estimator, bloggenauto tracking, pandectes, fontify; Google Fonts CSS for Poppins (18 variants) + Bebas Neue. DOM-reading agents (Claude in Chrome: page text/DOM; ChatGPT: ARIA tree) pay for every node; duplicated controls (3 localization selectors, quick-buy forms on every card) multiply the choices an agent must disambiguate.
findings.affected_scope: all pages; heaviest on home, `/collections/all`, `/search`. - Recommendation (theme + apps, merchant-controlled): uninstall or disable unused app embeds (Theme editor → App embeds: confirm each of koala gifts, pop-convert, dondy, estimator, affiliate, bloggenauto tracking is still wanted); turn off "quick buy" on product cards for the home page sections (removes 9 forms/≈30 buttons); hide the localization selectors (one real market); cut Poppins to the 3–4 weights actually used (Impact theme typ
findings.recommendation: (theme + apps, merchant-controlled): uninstall or disable unused app embeds (Theme editor → App embeds: confirm each of koala gifts, pop-convert, dondy, estimator, affiliate, bloggenauto tracking is still wanted); turn off "quick buy" on product cards for the home page sections (removes 9 forms/≈30 buttons); hide the localization selectors (one real market); cut Poppins to the 3–4 weights actually used (Impact theme typography settings); keep Judge.me but load its widget only on product pages. Target: home < 350 KB HTML, ≤ 40 scripts; product page < 250 KB.
findings.falsifiability: `curl -s https://primesupplements.ro/ | wc -c` and `grep -c "<script"` fall below the targets; `forms_total` on home ≤ 4.
findings.leading_indicator: HTML bytes and script count per template after each change.

findings.title: WebMCP: Shopify's adapter is present; no merchant tools, no form annotations (opportunity, platform-covered)
findings.evidence: every analysed page contains an inline 1,144-char loader: `function u(){return typeof(o.modelContext||r.navigator?.modelContext)?.registerTool=="function"} … e.src=c … s("//primesupplements.ro/cdn/shopifycloud/storefront/assets/storefront/webmcp-f427de6a.js","sha256-ypGF+5vIq4Psw4WG7nsVtdd/TCfsJWnrNuACdqLCElY=")` keyed on `localStorage "shopify:webmcp_adapter_loaded"` and waiting for `#shopify-origin-trials` (`origin_trials-318ab40a.js`, async, SRI). `standard-actions.js` is loaded as a module (`data-source-attribution="shopify.standard_actions"`). `webmcp_markers = {modelContext: 2, registerTool: 1, toolname=: 0, tooldescription=: 0}`; 0 `<meta http-equiv="origin-trial">` in the HTML (the OT script injects it); 13 forms on home / 7 on product pages carry no `toolname`/`tooldescription`. Which tools the adapter registers was not observable here (needs a WebMCP-capable browser or PSI).
findings.recommendation: do not write custom imperative tools that duplicate Shopify's (search, cart, checkout are covered by the adapter and by UCP); if a custom tool is ever added (e.g. "calculate protein dose" from the creatina/custom page), bind it to the existing form handler, mark purchases `consequentialHint: true` with a human confirmation step, and register on `document.modelContext` with `navigator.modelContext` fallback. Do not add declarative `toolname`/`tooldescription` piecemeal: partial annotation turns `webmcp-schema-validity` into a counted audit that scores 0.5 (fail) when any parameter lacks a description. When PSI quota allows, read `webmcp-registered-tools` from `lighthouse_agentic.py` to see the adapter's tool list and any schema issues.
findings.falsifiability: PSI `webmcp-registered-tools` lists Shopify tools; `webmcp-schema-validity` = 1.
findings.leading_indicator: n/a.

findings.title: UCP/MCP advertisement inconsistencies and generic tool metadata (Shopify-managed; depth → seo-ecommerce)
findings.evidence: `/.well-known/ucp` declares the MCP `endpoint` and both `supported_versions` URLs on `https://primesupplements1.myshopify.com/…`, while robots.txt and agents.md tell agents to `POST https://primesupplements.ro/api/ucp/mcp`; both answer `tools/list` identically (200, 177,661 B, 13 tools), so nothing breaks, but an agent that pins the origin from `/.well-known/ucp` transacts on the myshopify host (cookies, logs and rate limits per origin). Tool descriptions are Shopify generic ("products from the online store, hosted on Shopify"), price examples in USD (43 "USD" vs 8 "RON" occurrences), and none of the 13 tools carries MCP `annotations` (`readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint` absent even on `complete_checkout`/`cancel_checkout`). Google Pay handler config has `"auth_jwt": ""`; permalink endpoint `https://primesupplements.ro/buy`; identity linking via `accounts.shop.app`.
findings.recommendation: nothing editable by the merchant in these documents; hand to `seo-ecommerce` (`ucp_check.py` when fetching works) to confirm `search_catalog` returns RON prices with `context.currency=RON`, that `dev.ucp.shopping.fulfillment` config (`method_combinations: [["shipping"]]`, no pickup) matches the store's real delivery options, and that Google Pay merchant onboarding is complete (empty `auth_jwt`). Merchant levers that change what the tools return: product data quality (AGENTIC-04 item 3).
findings.falsifiability: `tools/call search_catalog {"query":"creatina","context":{"currency":"RON","address_country":"RO"}}` returns RON prices and complete product fields.
findings.leading_indicator: n/a.

findings.title: Seven MNX product descriptions contain pasted Gemini chat-UI markup, exposed to agents via HTML, `/products.json` and UCP `get_product`
findings.evidence: live `/products.json?limit=1` → product `mnx-hoodie-xforce-2-0-black` `body_html` starts with `<div class="markdown markdown-main-panel md-content enable-luminous-fast-follows enable-updated-hr-color stronger" id="model-response-message-contentr_294d1e7a3547cfff" dir="ltr"><div><b data-path-to-node="0" data-index-in-node="0">…`. Scan of all 185 product bodies (`$R/shopify/products-p*.json`): 7 products match `model-response-message|data-path-to-node|markdown-main-panel` — incl. `mnx-hoodie-motion-burgundy`, `mnx-hoodie-industrial-bronze`, `mnx-hoodie-industrial-dusty-rose`, `mnx-men-s-lightweight-hoodie-aesthetic-dove`, `mnx-mens-lightweight-hoodie-aesthetic-black`, `mnx-hoodie-xforce-2-0-black`. The wrapper ids/attributes are Google Gemini's response-panel DOM, i.e. the description was copy-pasted from a chat window with its UI markup.
findings.affected_scope: 7 of 185 products (all MNX apparel), on the product page, in `/products/{handle}.json` and in every MCP catalog response.
findings.recommendation: open each product in Shopify Admin → description → "Show HTML" and replace the body with clean paragraphs/lists (no `data-*` attributes, no `id="model-response…"`); while there, write real descriptions for the 89 MNX products with < 50 words (context) so `search_catalog` has something to match on.
findings.falsifiability: `curl -s "https://primesupplements.ro/products.json?limit=250" | grep -c "data-path-to-node"` = 0.
findings.leading_indicator: the 7 handles no longer match the pattern in a fresh Admin export.

findings.title: Duplicate /ro-hu/ market doubles the URL surface agents must crawl under a rate-limited WAF
findings.evidence: sitemap index lists 6 `/ro-hu/` child sitemaps (575 duplicate URLs of 1,151 total, `$R/sitemap.xml`, `$R/sitemaps/all-urls.txt`); the Hungary market serves identical Romanian content in RON (context). Combined with AGENTIC-03 (429 after bursts) an agent that follows the sitemap or hreflang alternates spends half its request budget on duplicates; `agents.md`/`llms.txt` never mention the market.
findings.recommendation: remove the Hungary market's web presence until Hungarian content and HUF pricing exist (TECH recommendation), which also removes the three localization forms/listboxes per page (AGENTIC-08, -12).
findings.falsifiability: sitemap index no longer lists `/ro-hu/` children; `/ro-hu/` returns 404/redirect.
findings.leading_indicator: sitemap URL count ≈ 576.

findings.title: Late-injected overlays (consent, popup, chat bubble, gifts) not tested for focus traps or cover; Lighthouse CLS unknown
findings.evidence: app embeds present in the HTML but rendered by JS: Pandectes GDPR banner (`pandectes-rules.js` is the first element in `<head>`, 8 `pandectes` matches on home), Pop Convert (`pop-convert-87/assets/main.js`), Dondy WhatsApp `ChatBubble.js`, Koala `gifts-embed.js` (120 KB), Judge.me widgets (117 `jdgm` matches). None could be rendered here (no Chromium). Their typical failure patterns (cookie layer persisting over controls, popup focus trap, chat bubble covering the mobile add-to-cart button, layout shift when they mount) are exactly the ones the agent-friendly-pages reference lists.
findings.recommendation: when a browser is available run `agent_ux_check.py https://primesupplements.ro/products/baton-proteic-capsuni --json` and `render_page.py … --a11y-tree`; verify on a 390 px viewport that after "Accept" the Pandectes layer has `pointer-events:none`/is removed, that the Dondy bubble does not overlap the sticky add-to-cart bar, and that Pop Convert does not trap focus. Measure CLS via PSI when quota allows (the Agentic Browsing fraction counts it).
findings.falsifiability: PSI CLS ≤ 0.1; a11y-tree snapshot shows no modal without a name and no focusable content behind `aria-hidden` after dismissal.
findings.leading_indicator: n/a.
